The chubby mouse was very proud of his special sauce. He wished he could make it again, but he knew it had been really lucky to find that special tomato.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved playing with his toy cars and trucks. One day, Tim's friend Ben came over to play. Ben brought a new toy with him. It was a toy gun, but Tim didn't like it because it looked like a weapon. 
"Let's play a game," said Ben. "We can set up a race track for our cars and see who wins."
Tim liked that idea, so they set up the race track. But when they finished, Ben took out his toy gun and started playing with it. Tim felt scared and guilty for playing with something that looked like a weapon. 
"I don't like that toy," Tim said to Ben. "It makes me feel scared."
"I'm sorry, Tim," said Ben. "I didn't mean to make you feel scared. Let's put it away and play with our cars instead."
Tim felt better and they continued playing with their cars. They had so much fun that they forgot all about the toy gun. From that day on, Tim and Ben played with their cars and trucks and never touched a weapon again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. Amy had a big yard with a purple swing. She loved to play outside and swing high in the sky.
One sunny day, Amy went to the yard with her friend, Max. Max saw the purple swing and said, "Wow! I want to swing too!" Amy smiled and said, "Okay, let's swing together!"
They took turns on the purple swing, laughing and having fun. They swung so high, they felt like they could touch the sky. After a while, they got tired and sat down on the soft grass. They looked at each other, happy to have spent the day swinging in the yard.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved Christmas because she got to see Santa and his reindeer. One day, Lily went outside to play in the snow. It was very wet and she got all wet too. 
As she was playing, she saw a reindeer stuck in the snow. "Oh no!" she said. "Reindeer, are you okay?" The reindeer tried to get up but it was too slippery. 
Lily ran inside to get her dad. "Dad, come quick! There's a reindeer outside and it's stuck in the snow!" Her dad came outside and saw the reindeer. "We have to help it," he said. They tried to push the reindeer out but it was too heavy. 
Just then, Santa came flying by in his sleigh. "Ho ho ho! What seems to be the problem?" he asked. Lily told him about the reindeer and Santa said he would help. He landed his sleigh and with his magic, he lifted the reindeer out of the snow. "Thank you, Santa!" Lily said. Santa smiled and said, "Merry Christmas!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she was running around and she stubbed her toe on a rock. It hurt a lot and she started to cry.
Her mom came over and asked, "What happened, Lily? Why are you crying?"
"I hurt my toe," Lily replied, still crying.
Her mom kneeled down beside her and looked at her toe. "It's just a little scrape, you'll be okay," she said.
Lily stopped crying and felt better. "I was being foolish and not looking where I was going," she said.
"That's okay, Lily," her mom said, "just be more careful next time." And with that, Lily went back to playing, being careful not to hurt her toe again.

John had been playing with his friends all day, but he was feeling hurt. He had mentioned to his friend, Tuesday, that he wanted to play a game with her, but she had ignored him. John was really sad and started to cry.
A kind lady noticed that John was upset and asked him what was wrong. John told her that Tuesday had not listened to him. He was really sad and didn't know what to do. 
The kind lady said that time would help make him feel better. She took John's hand and mentioned to him that it was Tuesday, the day of the week when anything can happen. "Maybe Tuesday will be a better day for you," she said. 
John felt a bit better and decided to go back and play with his friends. Sure enough, when he went back, Tuesday asked if he wanted to play a game with her. John smiled and said yes.
John was so happy that despite feeling hurt, Tuesday still wanted to be his friend. They had lots of fun together and never mentioned the hurt feelings again.

Once upon a time, there was a horse named Brownie. Brownie lived in a big stable with his horse friends. The stable was very dark at night, but Brownie was not scared. He liked to sleep and dream about running in the fields. 
One day, Brownie's friend Billy got lost in the woods. Brownie heard Billy shout for help. He knew he had to do something. Brownie ran out of the stable and into the woods. He searched and searched until he found Billy. 
Billy was so happy to see Brownie that he shouted with joy. Brownie was happy too. He led Billy back to the stable where all of their friends were waiting. They were happy to see Billy and they all shouted with joy. From that day on, Brownie felt very proud of himself for being a brave horse.

Jenny and John were walking in the park one day. They saw a machine and Jenny became excited. "Let's play on it," said Jenny.
John saw how competitive the machine was and said, "Do you think you can beat it?"
Jenny smiled and said confidently, "Yes, I can beat it. Watch me!"
But as soon as Jenny started playing, the machine started to make loud noises and lights flashed on it. As it got louder, Jenny got scared and ran away. 
John laughed and went to the machine. He played and beat it easily. Jenny was surprised and said, "You really scared the machine!"

Once upon a time there was a lazy caterpillar. It wanted to fly like the birds but it did not have wings. So the caterpillar asked its mom if it could get wings. 
Mom said she knew a place that might make it possible. She said, "You need to go to the airport." So the caterpillar went to the airport and asked the people there for help.
The airport people said they could help the caterpillar. They gave the caterpillar a special seat on a plane. The caterpillar was so happy! The seat was very comfortable and the caterpillar flew for hours and hours.
The caterpillar looked out of the window and saw so many new places. Finally, it arrived at its destination - a place with many beautiful butterflies flying around. 
The caterpillar was so happy it could finally fly like the butterflies. It thanked the airport people for all their help. From then on it could fly wherever it wanted. The lazy caterpillar's dream had finally come true!

Once upon a time there was a wealthy boy. He was very mean and loved to tease the other children. One day, he was playing with a shiny pin. He went to the park to find someone to tease.
He soon found a little girl, who was only three. The boy thought it would be fun to tease her with the pin. He showed the girl the pin, and she was so excited. She started to laugh and smile.
But then, the wealthy boy teasing her with the pin got too close. He accidentally poked the little girl with the pin! Ouch! The girl started to cry. She had never felt such pain.
The wealthy boy was scared. He ran away from the park, leaving the little girl all alone. He did not apologize or even look back. 
The little girl was so sad and scared. She had never been teased like that before. She never wanted to see the wealthy boy again. 
The end.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys and books. One day, Anna has a new toy. It is a kite. The kite has a long string and a tail. It is red and yellow and blue.
"Can I borrow your kite?" Ben asks Anna. He wants to fly the kite in the sky.
"Okay, but be careful," Anna says. She gives Ben the kite and the string. "Do not let go of the string. The kite will fly away."
Ben takes the kite and runs to the field. He throws the kite in the air. The wind makes the kite go up and up. Ben feels the string pull in his hand. He smiles. The kite looks like a bird.
Anna watches Ben from the bench. She sees the kite fly high and far. She sees the string get smaller and smaller. She feels sad. She misses her kite.
"Ben, come back!" Anna calls. "It is time to go home. Give me back my kite."
But Ben does not hear Anna. He is too busy with the kite. He does not see how distant the kite is. He does not notice that the string is loose. He does not feel the string slip from his hand.
The kite flies away. The string falls to the ground. Ben looks up and sees nothing. He feels sad. He lost the kite.
"Anna, I am sorry," Ben says. He runs to Anna with the string. "I did not mean to lose your kite. It was an accident."
Anna is angry. She does not want the string. She wants her kite. She does not forgive Ben. She does not want to be his friend.
They go home. They do not talk to each other. They do not play with toys and books. They are lonely and unhappy. They wish they had their kite and their friend.

Alice had a special mission. She was going to study at the park. She brought her pencil and paper, and was excited to find out what she would learn. She walked to the park and saw lots of different plants and birds. She wanted to know what each one was called.
Alice sat by a tree and started drawing pictures of the animals. She studied the the leaves and shapes of each one. She also looked at the colour of the feathers on the birds.
Alice noticed something else in the park. It was full of children playing and laughing. She soon realized that the park was a useful place to learn as well! She watched how the children played with each other and came up with games and stories of their own.
Alice was glad she came to the park. She had learned so much about plants, animals and making friends. Her day of studying had been fun and useful.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little girl named Ruby. She didn't have a lot of money, but she was very brave. One day,Ruby saw an old shield in the street. She knelt down to pick it up and noticed that it was heavy. 
Ruby decided to take the shield home with her. She got an old stick and used it as a handle. She then took the shield and leaned it against the wall. 
When Ruby went to bed that night, she felt a little bit safer. She knew the shield would help protect her in case anything bad happened. 
The next day, Ruby went to the park with her shield. She was so proud to show it off to her friends. She even pretended to be a knight and ran around, trying to keep everyone safe with her old shield. 
Ruby kept the shield as protection for many years. It made her feel safe and brave, even when things were scary. 
The end.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit and a turtle. The rabbit said to the turtle, "Let's race!" The turtle shook his head and smiled.
The two animals lined up, ready to start the race. The rabbit took off at a very fast speed! But at the end, the turtle was winning.
The rabbit was so frustrated that he ran faster, but he was still too slow. The turtle crossed the finish line first. The rabbit was so angry that he started kicking the ground.
The turtle said, "Be careful! That ground is very harsh!" But the rabbit was too mad to listen. He continued to kick until he hurt his feet.
The turtle sighed and said, "That's the end of the story." He was sad for the rabbit but was thankful for his own safety.

Once upon a time, there was a happy dog named Spot. Spot loved to run and play with his friends in the park. One day, Spot's owner took him for a walk and they saw a little girl with a cheerful smile. The little girl was wearing a pretty dress with a buckle on it.
Spot wanted to say hello to the little girl, so he wagged his tail and walked over to her. The little girl was so happy to see Spot and she started to clap her hands. Spot was so excited that he barked and jumped up and down. The little girl laughed and petted Spot's head.
Spot and the little girl became friends and they would often meet in the park to play. Spot loved his new friend and he would always wag his tail and bark happily whenever he saw her. The little girl would always wear her pretty dress with the buckle on it and they would clap and play together all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to help her mom in the kitchen. One day, Sue's mom asked her to get a teaspoon. Sue looked and looked, but she could not find one. She felt sad because she wanted to help.
The next day, Sue's mom told her she needed to spread some jam on bread for lunch. Sue remembered that she could not find a teaspoon the day before. She thought that maybe she could find one today. She looked in all the places she could think of, but there was still no teaspoon available.
Finally, Sue had an idea. She went to her toy box and found a tiny spoon from her toy tea set. She brought it to her mom and said, "I found a teaspoon!" Her mom smiled and said, "That's perfect!" Sue was so happy that she could help. She used the tiny spoon to spread the jam on the bread. From that day on, the tiny spoon from her toy tea set became their special teaspoon for spreading jam.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she saw a blue butterfly and wanted to catch it. She ran after it, but she didn't watch where she was going and fell down. 
Lily started to cry because she hurt herself. Her mom came outside and asked, "What happened, sweetie?" Lily said, "I fell down and it hurts, please make it better." 
Her mom picked her up and said, "Let's go inside and make sure you're safe." They went inside and put a bandaid on Lily's knee. Her mom said, "Next time, be careful when you run so you don't get hurt." 
Lily felt better and went back outside to play. She saw the blue butterfly again and remembered what her mom said. She walked slowly and carefully towards it and finally caught it in her hands. She was so happy and said, "Thank you, butterfly, for being my friend."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play outside in the park. One day, she saw a beautiful butterfly. "Look, mommy! A pretty butterfly!" she said. "Can we bring it home?" 
"No, Lily. The butterfly belongs in the world outside," her mommy replied. 
Lily was sad, but then she saw a colorful flower. "Mommy, this flower is so attractive! Can we bring it home?" 
"No, Lily. The flower belongs in the world outside, too. It needs sunshine and rain to grow," her mommy explained. 
Lily understood and continued to play in the park, enjoying the beauty of the world around her.

Once there was a little girl named Mary. She loved to choose her own clothes each day. She put on her rain boots and said, "Today I choose the yellow boots!"
Mary ran outside on a fair day to play in the rain. She ran and the rain hit her cheeks and she laughed. She spun around in the rain and jumped in the puddles. She smiled and said, "This day is really fair!"
The rain began to stop, so Mary ran back inside before she got too wet. She changed out of her yellow rain boots and chose a pretty dress and matching shoes. Then she smiled and said, "Now I'm ready for my fair day!"

Fred was a young boy of three. He liked to play and have fun. One day, Fred was getting dressed when he found a new shirt in his drawers. He put it on and it fit him perfectly. He was so excited to wear his brilliantly coloured new shirt.
The shirt was so bright, Fred felt like he was a superhero. He liked his new shirt so much, he even paraded around the kitchen to show it off to his mum and dad. His mum and dad smiled and said that the shirt was brilliant; it suited him perfectly. Fred smiled back and went back to playing.
He couldn't wait to show off his new shirt to all his friends. He was sure they would think it was brilliant too. Every time he put it on he felt special, like he could do anything.
And that's how Fred's new brilliant shirt fit into his life, making him feel like a superhero even at 3 years old.

Once there was a little boy, named Dan. Dan was three years old and lived with his mom and dad. Every Tuesday morning, Dan would get out of bed early. He liked Tuesdays because they were always fun, and usually something special would happen on Tuesdays.
Today was a Tuesday. Everything outside was gray and quiet. Dan went down to the kitchen. His mom had made him a special breakfast. It was Dan's favorite: cereal with milk and blueberries.
After breakfast, Dan and his mom went to the park. Dan loved playing in the park. He ran around, exploring and finding all kinds of new things. Dan only stopped running when he got tired. Sooner or later, he would take a break and sit in one of the swings.
Dan had a great time at the park, but eventually it was time to go home. As they were walking back, his mom said, "Dan, today was Tuesday and we had a lot of fun. Tomorrow will be Wednesday and there will be more fun! 
Dan smiled, happy that he had been able to get out and enjoy a fun special Tuesday.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. He loved to play with his red ball. One sunny day, Tom went outside to play with his ball in the land near his home.
Tom kicked the ball high in the sky. The ball went far, far away. Tom was sad because he could not find his ball. He walked and walked, looking for it. The land was big and sometimes dangerous. Tom knew he had to be careful.
At last, Tom found his ball near a big tree. He was very happy. Tom knew he should not kick the ball too hard next time. He went back home, holding his ball tightly. Tom played safely in his yard, away from the dangerous land.

Lila and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and swing on the swings. They saw a big tree with many branches. Some branches were low and some were high.
"Look, Ben, I can pull this branch!" Lila said. She grabbed a low branch and pulled hard. The branch was old and dry. It broke with a loud snap. Lila fell on the grass.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Lila cried. She hurt her hand and her knee. Ben ran to her and helped her up.
"Are you okay, Lila?" Ben asked. He saw blood on her hand and her knee. He felt sorry for her.
"I'm not okay, Ben. It hurts a lot." Lila said. She was sad and scared. She wanted her mom.
"Let's go find your mom, Lila. She can make you feel better." Ben said. He held her hand and walked with her. He saw a bench where Lila's mom was sitting. He called her name.
"Mom, mom, Lila needs you!" Ben shouted. Lila's mom heard him and saw them. She saw Lila's hand and knee. She got up and ran to them.
"What happened, Lila? What happened, Ben?" Lila's mom asked. She hugged Lila and looked at her wounds.
"Lila pulled a branch and it broke and she fell." Ben said. He told her what happened.
"Oh, Lila, I'm sorry. That was a bad branch. Let me clean your hand and your knee. It will sting a little, but it will help." Lila's mom said. She took out a tissue and some water and some band-aids from her bag. She cleaned Lila's hand and knee and put band-aids on them.
"Thank you, mom. Thank you, Ben." Lila said. She felt a little better. She smiled at her mom and her friend.
"You're welcome, Lila. You're a brave girl. And thank you, Ben, for being a good friend." Lila's mom said. She smiled at them both.
"Can we still play, mom?" Lila asked.
"Sure, Lila, but be careful. Don't pull any more branches, okay?" Lila's mom said.
"Okay, mom. I won't pull any more branches." Lila said.
Lila and Ben went back to play. They had fun in the park. They did not pull any more branches. They played until it was time to go home.

Ben and Mia love to go to the zoo with their mom and dad. They like to see the animals and learn their names. They have a favorite animal: the parrot. The parrot is famous because it can talk. It can repeat what people say.
One day, they go to the zoo and find the parrot in its cage. They say hello to the parrot and wait for it to talk. But the parrot is quiet. It does not repeat anything. Ben and Mia are sad. They wonder why the parrot is not talking.
They ask their mom and dad. Their mom and dad say that the parrot is shy. It does not like to talk when there are many people around. They say that the parrot needs some time and space to feel comfortable. They say that if they are patient and gentle, the parrot might talk to them.
Ben and Mia decide to try. They sit on a bench near the cage and watch the parrot. They talk to the parrot softly and kindly. They say things like "You are a beautiful parrot" and "We are your friends". They do not yell or make loud noises. They do not touch the cage or throw things at the parrot.
After a while, the parrot starts to move its head and look at them. It opens its beak and makes a sound. Ben and Mia are happy. They listen carefully. The parrot says "Hello, beautiful parrot". It repeats what they said. Ben and Mia clap their hands and laugh. They say "Hello, parrot" and "We are happy to meet you". The parrot repeats them too. It says "Hello, parrot" and "We are happy to meet you". Ben and Mia and the parrot have a fun conversation. They are all happy. The parrot is not shy anymore. It is famous and friendly.

Mum had a new table. It was soft and safe. Mum looked at it and smiled.
Mum said it was time to pay for the table. She gave the man some money. He said thank you and gave her a big hug. 
Mum and the little girl put their things on the table. They were so happy. They played with their toys and laughed together.
Mum said the table made them feel safe. Mum said it was their special table. 
The little girl liked to play with her toys at the safe table. Every day when she came home she went straight to it. She was happy to have such a nice safe table.

Once upon a time there was a kind little girl who loved to play. One day, she found a big trunk and decided to open it. Inside, she saw lots of toys. She smiled and ran to tell her mom.
Her mom was very happy and asked the little girl to help fill the trunk with all her toys. The girl was excited and quickly started taking out all her toys, one by one and placing them all in the trunk. 
She even found some of her old toys in the trunk, forgotten and still in good condition. When she was all finished, the trunk was filled with all kinds of toys - big ones, small ones, old ones and new.
The little girl was so proud. She hugged the trunk and thanked her mom for the surprise. 
Moral of the story: Kindness always brings joy.

Once upon a time, there was a little beetle. He was very small and had a hard shell that protected him from danger. One day, he saw a piece of candy on the ground and wanted to eat it. But the candy was too heavy for him to lift.
He tried and tried, but he couldn't lift it. Then, a big beetle came along and saw the little beetle struggling. The big beetle offered to help and lifted the candy for him. The little beetle was very grateful and thanked the big beetle.
The moral of the story is that sometimes we need help from others, and it's okay to ask for it. We should also be willing to help others when they need it.

Once upon a time, in a far off land there lived a Queen. The Queen was a kind Queen who always looked out for the people of her kingdom.
One day, the Queen heard a loud noise coming from the nearby forest and she panic. She ran to see what the noise was, but it was so dark and dangerous. She slowly crept through the forest, but then she heard a roar.
The Queen screamed and ran. She frantically searched for a way to get away from the scary sound. She soon stumbled upon a hole in the ground. She jumped in and it was deep and dark. The Queen found that she was safe and sound.
The Queen stayed there until morning, when it was safe to go outside. When she finally emerged the Queen thanked the stars that she was safe. Then she hurried home and told her people to be careful when they go near the forest.

Once upon a time there lived a very patient little bear. He lived in a small cave deep in the forest. One day, the bear thought he'd make something to eat so he took out a big pot and his special stick. He filled the pot with some delicious ingredients and put it onto the stove. 
When the bear started to stir the mixture, he heard a noise coming from the pot. He stopped stirring, wondering what it could be. Out of the pot popped a little mouse. 
The bear said, "hello, what do you want?" 
The little mouse replied, "I wanted some of the yummy food you are cooking!" 
The bear was so patient and kindly said, "of course you can! Take as much as you'd like!" 
The mouse was so happy and thanked the bear as he helped himself to some food. After the mouse left, the bear continued stirring his food. He was sure glad to be so patient.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat blueberries because they tasted sweet and yummy. One day, she went to the store with her mom to buy some blueberries. When they got home, Lily's mom told her to share the blueberries with her little brother, Max.
Lily didn't want to share because she was feeling grumpy. She wanted to eat all the blueberries by herself. But then, her mom said, "Lily, it's important to share with others. It will make them happy and you will feel happy too."
Lily thought about what her mom said and decided to share the blueberries with Max. They both ate the blueberries and had fun together. In the end, Lily realized that sharing is important and it made her feel happy too.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and watch the pretty colors in the sky when the sun went down. That was called a sunset. 
One day, Lily's mom made her a yummy snack. It was a big, juicy apple. Lily took a bite and it tasted so good! She loved the way it tasted. 
Later that day, Lily and her mom went on a walk. They saw some birds flying in the sky and some flowers growing in the grass. Lily thought it was all so crazy and fun. 
As the sun started to go down, Lily and her mom sat on a bench and watched the sunset. It was so beautiful with all the colors in the sky. Lily thought it was the best day ever!

Once upon a time, there was a big and happy family who loved to play games together. One day, they decided to play a game called "Snake and Ladders" on a large board. The family was having so much fun, but then something happened. The youngest child, Lily, accidentally knocked the board over, and all the pieces went flying everywhere. 
At first, everyone was upset and angry with Lily. But then, they thought about it and realized that it was just an accident. They decided to work together to pick up all the pieces and put the board back together. It was a big job, but they did it! 
In the end, the family learned that accidents happen and it's important to forgive and work together to fix things. They also learned that playing games together is a great way to have fun and spend time as a family.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved oatmeal for breakfast every day. He would pour the oatmeal into his bowl and eat it fast.
One day, Timmy's mom asked him if he wanted oatmeal for breakfast. Timmy said yes and his mom poured the oatmeal into his bowl. Timmy ate it fast and said, "Yum, that was good!"
After breakfast, Timmy went outside to play. He saw his friend Billy and said, "Want to play catch?" Billy said yes and they started to play. Timmy threw the ball fast and Billy tried to catch it, but he missed and fell down.
Billy started to cry and Timmy felt bad. He said sorry and helped Billy up. But then, Timmy's foot got stuck in a hole and he fell down too. He hurt his arm and had to go to the hospital.
Timmy learned that playing too fast can be dangerous and he promised to be more careful next time.

Once there was a monkey named Tom. He was a very graceful monkey and he was always looking for new adventures. So one day, he decided to travel to the jungle. His mum said he had to get her permission first, so he asked and she permitted him to go.
Tom was so excited that he started to dance and jump around. He ran off to the jungle right away!
When he got there, he saw lots of things. He saw exotic birds, big snakes and colourful flowers. Tom was having so much fun!
Then he saw a graceful monkey in a tree. She was doing somersaults and playing with the tree branches. Tom wanted to join in the fun, so he climbed up the tree and introduced himself.
The two monkeys spent the day playing together. They chased each other through the trees and sang silly songs. Tom had the best time!
At the end of the day, Tom said goodbye to his new friend and ran back home. His mum was so happy to see him. She gave him a big hug and said he was always welcome to go on more adventures. Tom was so happy!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved flowers and had a pretty vase in her room. One day, her mom asked her to wash the vase. Lily didn't want to do it because she was feeling grumpy. But her mom said it was important to keep the vase clean so the flowers would stay healthy. 
Lily took the vase to the sink and used soap and water to wash it. It was hard work, but she did it all by herself. When she was finished, she felt proud of herself for doing a good job. 
Later that day, Lily's mom brought home some beautiful flowers and put them in the vase. Lily smiled and felt happy. She realized that washing the vase was worth it because it made her room look pretty and made her feel good inside.

Once upon a time, there was a poppy. It was a pretty flower with a red color. One day, a bee came to the poppy and zoomed around it. The bee liked the poppy because it was sweet. 
But then something weird happened. The poppy started to shake and dance. The bee got scared and flew away. The poppy was not hurt, it was just having fun. 
From that day on, the poppy would often dance and zoom around. The other flowers thought it was weird, but they still liked the poppy. And the bee would come back to visit, but this time it would watch from a safe distance. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved roses and always wanted one for herself. One day, she saw a beautiful rose in her neighbor's garden and wanted it badly. She went to her neighbor and said, "I want your rose, please give it to me." 
The neighbor replied, "I'm sorry, but this rose is mine. You can't have it." Lily became very sad and miserable. She cried and cried because she wanted the rose so much. 
The next day, Lily decided to take the rose without asking for permission. She went to the neighbor's garden and picked the rose. But as soon as she picked it, she realized that it was wrong. She felt guilty and scared. 
When the neighbor found out, she was very angry and called Lily's parents. Lily's parents were disappointed and scolded her for taking something that wasn't hers. Lily learned that it's not right to take things that belong to others and that it's always better to ask nicely.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very good at drawing and everyone said she was gifted. One day, her mommy told her that if she drew a picture of their house, she would get a prize. Lily was very excited and started drawing right away. She worked very hard and finally finished her picture. Her mommy was very happy with it and gave her a big hug. She also gave her a prize, which was a yummy cookie. 
Later that day, Lily's little brother Jack broke her favorite toy. She was very angry and wanted to punish him. But her mommy told her that it's not nice to punish others and that they should forgive each other. So, Lily forgave Jack and they played together again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lily. Lily was 3 years old and loved to ride her bicycle. Everyday, Lily would gleefully step outside on her bicycle and she even had a special place to ride it.
One day, the sun was especially warm, so Lily decided to cycle for an extra long time. When she eventually stepped back into her house, Lily noticed that her mother was worried.
"Lily," said her mother. "It's not always good to take too many steps without listening to another's advice."
Lily smiled and nodded her head. She understood her mother's words and never stepped outside to ride her bicycle without telling someone first.
By following her mother's advice, Lily was always safe, warm and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and eat yummy snacks. One day, her mommy made her a delicious lunch with a sandwich and some fruit.
But when Lily tried to eat her sandwich, she got frustrated because it was too big to fit in her mouth. She tried to take a bite, but it just fell apart. So, she decided to eat her fruit instead.
After lunch, Lily went to play with her toys. She was playing with her toy stove and accidentally touched the hot burner. It burned her little finger and she cried out in pain. Her mommy came to help her and put some cool water on her finger to make it feel better. From that day on, Lily was very careful around the toy stove and never touched the burners again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big, generous dog named Max. Max had a pretty bow on his neck. He liked to play and share with his friends. One day, Max and his friends wanted to celebrate because it was his birthday.
Max said, "Let's have a party!" His friends were happy and said, "Yes, let's celebrate!" They played games and ate yummy food. Max shared his toys with everyone. They were all having a good time.
But then, Max saw a big cake. He wanted to eat it all by himself. He forgot to share with his friends. Max ate the whole cake very fast. After eating the cake, Max felt sick. His friends were sad because they didn't get any cake. Max learned that it is important to share with friends, even on his birthday.

Once upon a time there was a rude girl called Helen. One day, Helen was playing with her scissors. She wanted to cut a picture of her best friend, Jack. But as she cut, her scissors got stuck! 
Helen was frustrated and she shouted at Jack. She was very rude to him. Jack didn't like it and he ran away.
Helen chased after him, holding her scissors. But Jack was too fast and he managed to escape. So Helen stopped running and just stood still. 
She couldn't believe she had been so rude. Suddenly, she saw Jack a few metres away, looking at her sadly. Helen slowly smiled and waved at him. Jack smiled back and waved. 
The situation had ended. Jack and Helen both realised that being rude wasn't nice. They hugged and made up, then went off to play together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was three years old and her name was Sally. One day, Sally saw a lady at the park. She had lots of toys and she asked Sally if she wanted to play with them. 
At first, Sally said 'Yes, please!' but suddenly she changed her mind. She thought the toys looked fake and she didn't want to play with them. So she refused the lady. 
The lady was very sad and asked Sally why she said 'No'. Sally said she didn't like fake toys.
The lady smiled and said that she understood. She gave Sally a big hug and said 'Thankyou for being honest and refusing the toys'. Then she said goodbye and left the park. 
Sally was happy that she stayed true to herself and refused the fake toys. She went home and played with her real toys instead. The end!

One day, Jimmy and his mom went on a walk. Jimmy was so excited! They went on a path through the woods. Jimmy had a special bag and in it were two special gears. As he walked, Jimmy started to lose one of the gears. 
He was upset, but his mom told him not to worry. They started to look for the lost gear. After a while, Jimmy saw a glimmer near some rocks and he ran to it! He was so happy and grateful because it was his lost gear! 
He and his mom put it back in his bag, and they went on their way back home. Jimmy was so happy that he had been able to find his lost gear and he was grateful to his mom for helping him find it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she saw a butterfly. The butterfly was very pretty and had many colors. 
Lily said, "Hello, butterfly! Can I play with you?" 
The butterfly said, "Yes, you can play with me. But I can't stay too long. I will melt if I stay in the sun too much." 
Lily said, "Oh no! I don't want you to melt. Let's go find some shade." 
They found a tree with lots of shade. The butterfly said, "Thank you for finding a shady spot for me. You are very kind." 
Lily smiled and said, "You're welcome. I like to help insects when they need it. I have some water available if you're thirsty." 
The butterfly drank the water and then flew away. Lily was happy that she could help the butterfly. She went back to playing outside, feeling proud of herself for being kind to the little insect.

Once upon a time, there was a brilliant gate. It was so tall it seemed to reach up to the sky! Every day, lots of animals would come to the gate looking for food.
An old man lived nearby, and he knew the animals were hungry. So every day, he would come to the gate with some food. He would spread the food around so all the animals could eat.
The animals were so happy! They would flock around the old man and the gate, dance through the grass and chirp and squeak with delight when the food was put down.
The old man would watch with a smile and wave goodbye as the animals happily ate the food he provided. He was so kind to feed them each and every day. The animals were so thankful for the old man's generosity and kindness.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and eat candy. One day, Timmy's mom took him to the store to buy him a new toy. Timmy saw a toy he really liked, but it was very expensive. His mom told him that they couldn't buy it because it was too cheap. Timmy didn't understand why something that was too cheap couldn't be bought.
Later that day, Timmy asked his mom why they couldn't buy the toy. His mom told him the truth, that they didn't have enough money to buy it. Timmy was sad, but he understood. He knew that his mom always answered his questions truthfully.

Once upon a time, there was a fish named Finn. Finn loved to swim in the big blue sea all day long. One day, Finn met a crab named Carl. Carl asked Finn, "Can you help me with my task? I need to find my lost shell." Finn said, "Sure, I can help you. Where did you see it last?" 
Carl said, "I saw it near a foolish octopus who likes to play tricks on me." Finn and Carl went to search for the shell. They found the octopus and asked him if he had seen the shell. The octopus said, "Yes, I have it. But I won't give it back unless you can beat me in a race." 
Finn and Carl agreed to the race. They swam as fast as they could and beat the octopus. The octopus gave back the shell and said, "You are not as foolish as I thought. I will not play tricks on you anymore." Finn and Carl were happy they completed their task and became good friends.

Once upon a time there was a lady who had a big dream. She wanted to carry her dream far away and make it come true. Every day the lady tried hard to make it happen, but the dream seemed so far away.
One day a kind man saw the lady trying so hard. He went to her and said, "Do not feel ashamed, I will help you carry your dream". The lady was so thankful to the kind man and together they began to make the dream come true.
Soon, the dream came true and the lady was so happy. The kind man had helped her in a very important way and she will always be thankful for his help.
This story teaches us that we should never feel ashamed to ask for help. Sometimes, asking for help can make our dreams come true.

Billy and Sarah joined hands and set off to explore the playground. Everything seemed so exciting; they ran around, joining the fun with all their friends.
The most exciting attraction was the slide - they ran up to it and joined the queue, eagerly awaiting their turn. When the time came, Sarah slid down first - and then it was Billy's turn.
He got to the top of the slide, and couldn't wait to slide down to the bottom. But, when he got to the bottom, Billy started to feel dizzy. He tried to stand up, but he couldn't. Sarah had expected Billy to join her, but he stayed lying on the ground and didn't move.
It was only then when Sarah realised that something was very wrong. Once the teachers and parents arrived, the truth quickly began to unfold: Billy had had a medical emergency, and he had been rushed by ambulance to the hospital.
Unfortunately, when Billy arrived at the hospital he had already passed away. The slide had been the last thing he ever did - it was the activity that had caused his dizzy feeling and the medical emergency that would take his life.

Tom and Lily were playing in the bathroom. They liked to pretend they were pirates and use the towels as sails and the brushes as swords. They saw a shiny thing on the sink. It was a razor. Tom wanted to play with it.
"Look, Lily, a treasure!" he said. "Let's see what it can do."
He picked up the razor and tried to cut the towel. But the razor was sharp and it cut his finger. He cried out in pain and dropped the razor. It broke into pieces and they scattered on the floor.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom shouted. "It hurts, it hurts!"
Lily ran to him and saw the blood on his finger. She was scared and sorry.
"Tom, I'm sorry, I'm sorry!" she said. "You shouldn't play with that. It's not a treasure, it's a razor. It's for grown-ups, not for kids. It's dangerous and disgusting."
She wrapped his finger with a tissue and hugged him. She heard their mom coming.
"Mom, mom, help!" she called. "Tom cut his finger with a razor. It was an accident, we were playing pirates."
Their mom came into the bathroom and saw the mess. She was angry and worried.
"What have you done?" she asked. "How did you get the razor? You know you're not allowed to touch it. It's very sharp and it can hurt you. Look at all the blood and the broken pieces. It's disgusting and unsafe. You could have cut yourself worse or stepped on them."
She took Tom and Lily to the kitchen and cleaned and bandaged Tom's finger. She gave them both a hug and a kiss.
"I'm glad you're okay, Tom," she said. "But you have to be more careful and listen to me. Razors are not toys, they are tools. And you have to respect them and leave them alone. Do you understand?"
Tom nodded and said he was sorry. He felt bad and stupid.
"I understand, mom," he said. "I'm sorry, mom. I won't play with razors again. I don't like them. They're disgusting and they hurt."
Lily nodded and said she was sorry too. She felt guilty and sad.
"I'm sorry, mom," she said. "I should have stopped Tom. I don't like razors either. They're disgusting and they scare me."
Their mom smiled and said she forgave them. She told them to be more careful and to play with safer things. She said she loved them and they were her treasures. She took them to their room and gave them some books and toys. They said they loved her too and they were sorry. They hugged and kissed her and said they would be good. They learned their lesson and never played with razors again.

Once upon a time, there were two brothers. The eldest brother was very good at trades, while the youngest brother liked to soak in the sun. Every day, the eldest brother would go out and make trades so that he could get nice things for his younger brother. To show his appreciation, the younger brother would also get up early in the morning and help his brother with his trades. 
On one such day, the two brothers went to a trading fair. There, they saw all sorts of nice things that they wanted. They spent the whole day trading and the elder brother managed to get some nice things for his younger brother.
When night came, the eldest brother asked his younger brother whether he was satisfied with the trades. The younger brother smiled and said that everything was just fine.
The following day, the younger brother asked his elder brother if he could go and soak in the sun for a bit. The elder brother smiled and said yes. As his younger brother ran off, the elder brother scratched his head and said aloud, "It's a good thing I made those trades yesterday." 
And, when the elder brother's younger brother came back, he brought the elder brother a fine gift. It was something that the elder brother had wanted at the trading fair the day before! 
The younger brother had gone to the trading fair and managed to make a trade on his own! The elder brother was so proud. From then on

Jenny was embarrassed. She sat in her chair and held her guitar. She had never played in front of so many people before. She didn't know what to do.
Suddenly, the music started playing. Jenny was so nervous she almost dropped her guitar. She gripped it tight and started to play. She was shaking and the notes were shaky at first.
But Jenny kept playing. She closed her eyes and started to get the hang of it. She finished the song and opened her eyes. Everyone was clapping and cheering! Jenny was so relieved.
Jenny smiled, put down the guitar and sat back down in her chair. She wasn't embarrassed anymore. She was so proud of herself for playing in front of all those people. She would never forget it.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty girl named Lily. She loved to play with her drum every day. One day, she was playing her drum in the park when a boy came up to her. "Can I play with your drum?" asked the boy. "Sure!" said Lily. 
The boy rubbed his hands together and started to play the drum. Lily was happy that she made a new friend. They played together for a while until the boy accidentally hit the drum too hard and it broke. "Oh no!" said Lily. "My drum is broken." 
Lily was sad because she loved her drum so much. She went home crying, and her mom asked her what happened. "My drum is broken," said Lily. Her mom tried to fix it, but it was too broken to be fixed. Lily was very sad and missed her drum very much. The end.

Once there was a brave fish who lived in the big deep blue sea. Every day he would swim happily in the sunny waters, looking for his friends. One day, he saw something unusual. It was a net!
The brave fish stayed very still. He could feel the net closing around him. He was going to be trapped! Suddenly, another fish swam up and said, "Let me help you!"
The brave fish smiled. Together, they worked to untangle the net so the brave fish could escape. Eventually, they were able to work the net free. The brave fish was so happy!
But then, the other fish began to tease him. "Why were you so scared of the net?" he said. The brave fish didn't know what to say! He was embarrassed that he'd been caught.
But then his friend said, "That was so brave of you to face the net." The brave fish smiled. He felt so happy and proud. He had faced the net, and he was free!

Once upon a time, there was a delicate jail. It was a special place that kept people safe. But one day, the jail would not open. No matter how hard the people tried, they could not unlock it. 
Then a brave little boy came along. He had a secret plan. He knew just how to unlock the delicate jail. Everyone watched him in awe as he carefully worked his magic.
He used his special key to unlock the jail. A giant cheer went up as the door opened. Everyone was happy to be free and ran off to play. The little boy had unlocked the delicate jail!

Once upon a time there was a little girl who was very curious about everything. She was always looking for new things to discover and explore. One day, she came across a box with a big red ribbon on it. Inside the box was a magic wand.
The little girl couldn't believe her eyes and immediately picked up the wand. She waved it around and said the magical words, "Abracadabra!" Suddenly, the wand began to glow and sparkle.
The girl was so excited that she began to laugh. She laughed and laughed until she accidentally broke the wand in two. "Uh oh," she said nervously.
Suddenly, a funny fairy appeared and said, "Don't be sad! I know how to fix it!" With one flick of her wand, the magic wand was fixed!
The girl was so happy to have her magic wand back that she danced around with glee. She thanked the fairy for helping her fix the broken wand and went on her way.

Once upon a time, there was a man who lived all by himself. Every day, he would look out the window of his house. One day, he saw something strange. It was a woman. She looked very happy, but the man did not know who she was. 
He asked his neighbor, but the neighbor said he did not know her. The man began to look for her every day. He looked in parks, in cafes, and in shops. But he could not find her. 
One day, he decided to try one last place. He looked in the temple, and there she was! The man was so shocked, he said hello to the woman. She said hello back and asked him why he was looking for her. The man said, “Because you are my wife!" The woman was very surprised. She had been looking for her husband too! They both were so happy, and the man knew his long search was finally over.

James was a 3 year old who loved to dress up every day. One day, he decided to dress in a crazy way; he wore his favourite green t-shirt, purple trousers and bright yellow shoes. James wanted to go to the library to show off his outfit, so he skipped all the way there. When he arrived at the library, he saw other people giving him strange looks.
Suddenly, James heard a grumpy voice shouting at him. It was the librarian. She told James that crazy clothes were not allowed in the library and he must go home and change his outfit if he wanted to stay. James became very upset and started to cry.
But then, the librarian had an idea. She told James he could borrow some library books and take them home to dress up the books instead. That way, he could still show off his crazy clothes. James was delighted! He quickly gathered up some books and went home with a smile on his face.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play dress-up and pretend to be a princess. One day, she found a shiny belt in her mom's closet. It was pink and had sparkles on it. "Mommy, can I wear this belt?" Lily asked.
Her mom said, "Sure, but be careful. That belt is fake, so it might not hold up well." Lily didn't understand what "fake" meant, but she put the belt on anyway.
As she twirled around in her princess dress, she noticed her dog, Max, following her. "Max, do you want to play with me?" she asked. Max barked and wagged his tail, so Lily knew he wanted to play too.
They played together all afternoon, with Max following Lily around and chasing after her. When it was time for dinner, Lily took off the belt and put it back in her mom's closet.
"Did you have fun playing dress-up, Lily?" her mom asked.
"Yes, and Max played with me too! He followed me everywhere!" Lily said with a smile.

Dave was excited because he just got a new toy. It was loud and colorful. He couldn't wait to show it to his friends.
Dave performed all sorts of tricks with his new toy. He spun the toy around and around. He twirled it around his head. He even pretended to juggle it with one hand.
Dave's friends thought his new toy was so cool. They all cheered for him when he performed. Dave was so proud of himself. His new toy was the best.
Dave had so much fun with his new toy. He wanted to play with it all day long. He was getting louder and louder. Finally, his mom had to say, "That's enough for now, Dave. Time for dinner!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved muffins! One day, she went to the bakery to buy a muffin. She saw a wealthy lady buying lots of muffins. 
Lily said, "Wow, you have so many muffins! Can I have one, please?" 
The wealthy lady replied, "No, I need all of them for myself." 
Lily felt sad and walked away. As she was walking, she saw a homeless man sitting on the street. He looked hungry. She thought of the muffin and decided to share it with him. 
She squeezed the muffin in half and gave one half to the homeless man. He smiled and said, "Thank you, little girl. You are very kind." 
Lily felt happy and learned that sharing is more important than being wealthy.

Once there was a boy named Fred. He was 3 years old. One day, he decided to invite his friends over for a playdate. He asked his mom for some olives to share with his friends.
Fred's mom gave him some olives and he put them on the table. He then went outside to wait for his friends to arrive.
It started to rain and soon the olives got wet. Fred was so disappointed!
Fred's friends still came over and he was really happy. He invited them to play in the rain and they had lots of fun.
After the playdate, the olives had dried out and Fred was able to eat some with his friends. They had a great time together!

Once upon a time, there was a chubby bunny named Benny. Benny loved to eat carrots and play in the fields. One day, Benny saw a beautiful flower and wanted to pick it. But his mommy told him that he shouldn't pick the flower because it was not nice to take things that didn't belong to him.
Benny didn't listen to his mommy and picked the flower anyway. Later that day, Benny's friend asked him where the flower came from. Benny felt sad and realized that he had made a mistake. He missed the flower and wished he could put it back where it belonged.
Benny learned that it was important to listen to his mommy and not take things that didn't belong to him. From that day on, he promised to be a good bunny and never take anything without permission.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat oysters, but they were very expensive. One day, Lily's mommy said she could pay for one oyster if she did her chores. Lily was very happy and worked very hard to earn the money.
Finally, Lily had enough money to buy her favorite oyster. She went to the store and bought it. But on the way home, she dropped it and it broke. Lily was very sad. She had paid for the oyster, but she didn't get to eat it. 
Lily looked up at the sky and saw a distant cloud. She wished she could go there and forget about her broken oyster. Suddenly, she felt better. She realized that sometimes things don't go as planned, but it's okay to be sad and move on.

Once upon a time there was a big dragon. It had a huge head and fire would come out of its mouth. The dragon lived high up in a mountain and it always looked very angry.
One day, a brave knight rode up to the mountain and stood in front of the dragon. He was ready to fight the dragon, but he did not have to. The dragon said "it is time for me to release the fire inside me".
The knight was surprised. He wanted to know how the dragon was going to do that. The dragon said "Just wait a little bit." So the brave knight waited.
And then, a huge burst of light surrounded the dragon. It was like its head opened up, and all the fire inside was released out into the world. The dragon smiled and it looked very happy.
The brave knight was amazed. He said "you look so different". The dragon said "Yes, now I am free". Then the knight and the dragon became good friends.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Sally. She was very honest and she loved taking pictures with her camera. 
One day Sally and her family went on a trip to a far away place. The moment they arrived, Sally immediately unpacked her camera so she could take pictures. 
Sally was so excited about all the new things she could take pictures of. She quickly moved around the area, taking picture after picture. 
However, when Sally returned to her family's house, she realized her camera was missing. She had been so eager to take pictures that she had forgotten to unpack her camera from her suitcase. 
Sally was sad and heartbroken, but she had learned an important lesson about being honest and responsible. Even if it means something bad happens in the end.

Once there was a fish who loved to bounce. Every day he would jump out of the water and bounce as high as he could. He was always so happy when he bounced.
One day the fish decided it would be fun to explore the world outside of the water. He jumped up and bounced out onto the land. He looked around and everything was so new and exciting.
Soon the fish got bored. Everything was so boring. He wanted to bounce again. So he found a big bendy tree and he bounced up and down it. It was so much fun bouncing on the tree and it made the fish smile. 
Eventually the fish had to go back to the water. He bounced into the water and felt so happy again. He knew he would always enjoy bouncing and exploring.

Once upon a time, there was a big kangaroo. He lived in a big field with lots of grass to eat. But one day, he got very hungry and couldn't find any food. He looked around and saw a little girl with a basket of apples. The kangaroo hopped over and asked if he could have an apple. The little girl was happy to feed the kangaroo and gave him a juicy apple. 
After eating the apple, the kangaroo felt uncomfortable. He had eaten too much and his tummy hurt. He lay down in the grass and closed his eyes. The little girl felt bad for the kangaroo and decided to stay with him until he felt better. They sat in the field together and watched the clouds go by. Eventually, the kangaroo's tummy felt better and he hopped away, feeling grateful for the little girl's kindness.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She was 3 years old and very brave. One day, Lucy decided to go exploring. She put on her light jacket, said goodbye to her family and set off.
As she wandered along, she heard a funny noise coming from behind a bush. She knelt down and peered through the leaves. What a surprise! It was a pin! Lucy thought it was beautiful and wanted to keep it. She reached in carefully and managed to grab it.
Suddenly, she heard a voice behind her. Startled, Lucy looked up to see a fairy. The fairy was wearing a sparkly dress and had light wings. She told Lucy that she wanted the pin back.
Lucy was so scared that she started to cry. The fairy was very kind and gently explained to Lucy that she needed the pin to help manage her magic. She asked Lucy if she would kindly give it back. Lucy wiped away her tears and managed to do it.
The fairy thanked her and waved her wand. As a reward for being so brave, Lucy received a special gift. Then the fairy waved her wand again and flew away, leaving Lucy with her surprise. 
The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lizzie. She went out for a walk in the woods one day. She looked up in the sky and saw a beautiful raven. She wondered why the raven was there. 
Lizzie continued walking and soon heard some noises in the trees. She was starting to feel a little scared, but she was brave and decided to go and take a look. As she walked closer, she saw a big black raven. It was calm and still looking at her. Lizzie was so scared she wanted to run away. 
Suddenly, the raven flew down from its perch in the tree and attacked Lizzie. Lizzie screamed and ran away. She ran as fast as she could until she was safe. She was so scared and scared of the raven she never went near the woods again. 
The raven screeched behind her, and the bad memory always stayed in her mind.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big sister named Emma who was very strong. One day, Lily wanted to try to lift a heavy frame all by herself. But she was too weak and the frame fell on her foot. She started to scream.
Emma heard her sister's scream and asked, "Lily, what happened? Are you okay?"
Lily said, "No, my foot hurts. The frame fell on it."
Emma helped Lily lift the frame off her foot and said, "You should ask for help if something is too heavy. It's okay to be weak sometimes." 
Lily nodded and said, "Thank you, Emma. You're strong and helpful." 
From that day on, Lily always asked for help when something was too heavy for her to lift.

Mum was in the kitchen, making dinner. It looked modern, with shiny surfaces and many gadgets. Mum was always in the kitchen and she looked very busy, rushing around.
One day she noticed that something was missing. She had a big lock on the door, and she couldn't open it. She kept pushing the button, but it wouldn't open.
Mum asked her little daughter for help. The girl knew what to do, so she stepped forward and put her hand on the lock. She smiled, moved the handle and it opened.
Mum was amazed. They went inside and the kitchen was exactly the same. It was just as modern - only now it had a lock. Mum was so happy to have something to keep the kitchen safe. 
The little girl smiled, proud that she had locked the kitchen.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy cars and trucks. One day, he found a new truck that he really liked. It was big and blue and had a telephone on the back.
Timmy's friend, Johnny, came over to play. Johnny brought his own truck to play with. It was also big and blue, but it didn't have a telephone on the back. Timmy said, "My truck is better because it has a telephone on the back. It's original."
Johnny didn't agree. He said, "My truck is better because it matches the color of the sky." Timmy didn't like that. He wanted his truck to be the best. They argued for a while, but then Timmy had an idea. He said, "Let's race our trucks and see which one is faster!" Johnny agreed.
They lined up their trucks and raced them down the hallway. Timmy's truck was faster, but Johnny's truck matched the color of the sky better. In the end, they both agreed that their trucks were special in their own way. They decided to play with both trucks together and have fun.

Jill and Tom went to the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and look for shells. They found many pretty shells of different colors and shapes. They put them in a bucket to take home.
"Look, Tom, I found an oyster!" Jill said, holding a big, gray shell. "Maybe there is a pearl inside!"
"Wow, let me see!" Tom said, running over to Jill. He wanted to see the pearl too.
They opened the oyster carefully, hoping to find a shiny, round pearl. But there was no pearl inside. Instead, there was a tiny crab, hiding in the oyster.
"Hello, little crab!" Jill said, smiling. "You are not a pearl, but you are cute!"
The crab waved its claws at Jill and Tom, as if to say hello back. Then it scuttled out of the oyster and into the water.
"Bye, little crab!" Tom said, waving. "Have fun in the sea!"
Jill and Tom were not sad that they did not find a pearl. They were happy that they made a new friend. They put the oyster back in the sand and looked for more shells. They were ready for more adventures.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was three years old and she had some pastels. She liked to use them to draw pictures.
One day she took out her pastels and started to draw. She made a big messy picture. The colours swirled together to make a rainbow. The little girl was very happy with her picture.
She wanted to show her family what she had done. But when the girl went show it to them the mess that she had made was too big. It was so messy that her family laughed.
The little girl was sad that her picture was a mess. She didn't want to use her pastels anymore. So she put them away and never used them again.
The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing in the park and looking at the fountain. The fountain was big and had water that went up and down. Timmy liked to watch the water go up and down slowly.
One day, Timmy saw a girl at the park. She looked sad and lonely. Timmy wanted to be her friend, but she didn't want to play with him. She ignored him and walked away. Timmy felt sad too.
Later that day, Timmy was playing near the fountain when he saw the girl again. She was trying to throw a coin in the fountain, but she couldn't reach. Timmy remembered how she ignored him earlier, but he still wanted to help her. He went over and helped her throw the coin in the fountain. The girl smiled and said thank you. Timmy felt happy that he helped her and they became friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Janey. She had a great big heart and a wonderful smile. Her parents noticed that she had been very gifted since she was very young.
One day Janey had an idea. She wanted to show her love for the world and asked her parents if she could get a permit. "What kind of permit do you need, sweetheart?" asked her mother. Janey replied with a big grin, "I want to give away free hugs to everyone!"
Her parents thought this was a great idea and they gave Janey a permit to hug. So, with the permit in hand, Janey set out on her mission. Everywhere she went, she hugged children, adults, and even animals, spreading her love and joy. 
The whole world was delighted that Janey was out spreading her love and gifts. Everyone was cheered up whenever they saw her. Janey even got hugs of appreciation in return. 
It was an amazing experience for Janey and her parents. Everyone was so happy and the love was contagious!

Once there was a little boy who really wanted a kayak. So he asked his mom and dad, but they said no. The little boy was really upset, so he decided to ask his Uncle for help. He found his Uncle and demanded that he get a kayak. Uncle was very reliable and said he would see what he could do.
The next day Uncle arrived with a big red kayak for the boy. The boy was thrilled and could not wait to try it out. So he ran to the lake and hopped in. He enjoyed paddling around with his new kayak. He was so happy that his Uncle had been so reliable and had found him such a cool present.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her backyard. One day, she found a cool hedge that she had never seen before. She wanted to explore it, but her mom said it wasn't safe.
Lily didn't understand why she couldn't play near the hedge. She asked her mom, but her mom just said it was too dangerous. Lily was sad because she really wanted to see what was on the other side.
Later that day, Lily's ball accidentally went over the fence and landed near the hedge. She knew she shouldn't go get it, but she really wanted her ball back. She decided to be brave and go get it.
As she got closer to the hedge, she heard a loud growling noise. She quickly realized that there was a big dog on the other side. She was scared, but she slowly backed away and ran back to her house. She finally understood why her mom said it wasn't safe to play near the hedge.

One day, the farmer grabbed his pitchfork and started to walk out to the barn. He opened the doors of the barn and inside were two big, brown bulls. The farmer was so excited that he clapped his hands together. 
The farmer shouted, "Who wants to be first? To go for a walk in the meadow and see the flowers and the trees?" 
The two brown bulls stamped their feet and started to dance around. The farmer bounded into the pen with them and started to push them to the door. He said, "Come on now, let's go outside together."
The two bulls raced ahead and soon the farmer and the bulls were out in the fresh air. They started to trot and play around in the meadow. The farmer watched the bulls with a smile on his face, he was so excited to see them in the meadow enjoying the scenery. 
The farmer and the two brown bulls stayed in the meadow playing and running around until they were too tired to go on. As they trotted back to the barn, the farmer smiled thinking how excited the two bulls had been.

Anna and Ben were at the park with their mom. They saw a vendor with a big cart of balloons. The vendor had many colors of balloons: red, blue, yellow, green, pink, and purple. Anna and Ben wanted a balloon each.
"Mom, can we have a balloon?" Anna asked.
"Sure, sweetie. You can choose one color each. What color do you want?" Mom said.
"I want a pink one!" Anna said.
"I want a blue one!" Ben said.
Mom gave the vendor some money and the vendor gave them a pink balloon and a blue balloon. Anna and Ben were very happy. They thanked the vendor and held their balloons tightly.
They walked around the park, looking at the flowers, the birds, the swings, and the slides. They saw other kids playing with their balloons too. Some kids let their balloons go up in the sky. Anna and Ben did not want to do that. They liked their balloons too much.
But then, a strong wind came and blew their balloons away. Anna and Ben were very sad. They cried and ran after their balloons. But they could not catch them. The balloons flew higher and higher until they disappeared.
"Mom, our balloons are gone!" Anna sobbed.
"I'm sorry, honey. The wind was too strong. Maybe we can get another balloon another day." Mom said.
She hugged Anna and Ben and tried to comfort them. But they still felt very uncomfortable. They missed their balloons a lot. They wished they could hold them again.

One day, Mary went to the store to pick some juice. She saw lots of different kinds of juice but she chose the apple juice. She grabbed a bottle and went to the check-out. The cashier was very friendly and calm.
After Mary left the store, she went home. There, she opened the bottle and took a sip. The juice was delicious! She smiled and drank some more.
When she finished the juice, she put the bottle in the sink. Then she washed her hands and went to her room to watch her favorite show. It was so nice and calm.
The next day, Mary went to the store again. She was excited to pick some more juice.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite doll that she loved very much. One day, Lily's little brother came and took the doll from her. Lily was very sad and cried a lot. She wanted her doll back.
Lily's mommy came and saw what happened. She asked Lily's brother to give the doll back to Lily. At first, he didn't want to, but then he saw how sad Lily was. So, he gave the doll back to Lily.
Lily was very happy and hugged her doll gently. She completed her tea party with her doll and her brother. They all had fun together. The end.

Once upon a time, a prince was walking through the forest. He was on a mission to find a beautiful palace to celebrate his birthday. As he walked further into the forest, he began to believe he had found the most perfect place in the world. The palace looked very fair. 
The prince entered the palace to explore and began to celebrate his special day. Suddenly he heard a loud, deep voice.
"Hello prince, you must leave this palace immediately."
The prince was scared and asked "why?" but received no reply. He reluctantly began to leave. As he walked away, he felt as if something bad was going to happen. 
The next day, the forest was burning and the palace was destroyed. Everyone was sad and thought the fire came from the palace. The prince had known it was dangerous, but it was too late - the fair palace was no more.

Once upon a time there was a boy. He went for a walk in the park and he saw a tree. He wanted to climb it, but it was so high! He was a brave boy, so he tried. He put his feet on the bark and climbed, and climbed, and climbed. Suddenly, the tree began to snap! The boy jumped off quickly, and he heard a loud noise behind him. The tree had fallen over and landed in a puddle! The boy was not hurt, but he noticed something else. There was a jar of yummy sauce spilled all over the ground! He knelt down and tasted it, and it was delicious. He took it home with him and ate it with all his meals. The sauce made everything taste so much better and the boy was very happy. He was proud that his brave climb of the high tree had brought him something so special!

Tom and Amy went to the port with their dad. They liked to observe the big boats and the people who worked on them. They saw a boat with a big crane that lifted boxes and put them on the dock. They saw another boat with a lot of flags that waved in the wind. They saw a boat with a lot of fish that smelled bad.
"Look, dad, look!" Tom said. "That boat has a lot of fish!"
"Yes, it does, Tom," dad said. "That boat is a fishing boat. The people on it catch fish and sell them to the market."
"Can we buy some fish, dad?" Amy asked.
"Maybe later, Amy," dad said. "First, let's go and see the cheerful boat."
"The cheerful boat?" Tom and Amy asked.
"Yes, the cheerful boat," dad said. "It's a boat that takes people for a ride and makes them happy. It has music and games and snacks. Do you want to go on the cheerful boat?"
"Yes, yes, yes!" Tom and Amy said.
Dad bought tickets for the cheerful boat and they got on board. They saw a lot of other people who were smiling and laughing. They heard a lot of songs and noises. They played with balls and balloons and puzzles. They ate popcorn and candy and ice cream. They had a lot of fun on the cheerful boat.
Tom and Amy observed the port from the cheerful boat. They saw the big boats and the people who worked on them. They saw the sun and the water and the birds. They felt the wind and the waves and the joy. They hugged their dad and thanked him for the wonderful day. They were very happy.

Sara and Tom were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big bunch of grapes on a table. They were hungry and wanted to eat some.
"Look, grapes!" Sara said. "Let's go and get some."
"But they are not ours," Tom said. "Maybe someone else will come back for them."
Sara did not listen. She ran to the table and grabbed a grape. She put it in her mouth. It was sweet and juicy. She was glad.
"Come on, Tom, they are yummy!" Sara said. "No one is here. We can have some more."
Tom was scared. He did not want to take what was not his. He looked around. He saw a man walking towards the table. He had a big hat and a big bag. He looked angry.
"Uh-oh, Sara, we have to move!" Tom said. "That man is coming. He is the owner of the grapes. He will be mad at us."
Sara did not hear him. She was busy eating more grapes. She did not see the man until he was right in front of her. He shouted at her.
"Hey, you little thief! What are you doing with my grapes? Give them back to me!"
Sara was scared. She dropped the grapes and ran away. Tom followed her. They hid behind a tree. They heard the man looking for them.
"Where are you, you little rascals? I will teach you a lesson!"
Sara and Tom were sorry. They wished they had not taken the grapes. They learned their lesson. They decided to never take what was not theirs again.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer called Bob. Bob loved to raise squash in his garden. Every day, Bob would spend hours taking care of his squash plants and tending to the garden.
One day, Bob was feeling especially grateful for his squash garden. He looked at all his squash plants and smiled. Bob said, "Thank you, squash plants, for blessing me with a wonderful harvest."
The squash plants seemed to understand Bob, because they gave a gentle nod in response. Bob was so happy with the squash plants that he wanted to give them a special treat.
Bob decided to raise a nice big bowl of squash soup for the plants. He carefully cut up the squash and cooked it in a pot. It smelled so delicious!
Bob fed the squash soup to the plants and thanked them for their hard work. The plants seemed to be very grateful for their reward. Bob was happy to share his love for squash with them.

Once upon a time there was a brave girl. She was always ready to try new things. One day, she decided to explore the woods. She ran and ran and soon found herself in a very wild area. The ground was rough and it was hard to move around.
The brave girl kept going until she arrived at a big wall made of logs. Behind it was a small house. She could see an old man inside. The old man looked very angry. He shouted at the brave girl and said she was breaking the law.
The brave girl was scared so she ran away. But she knew she had to go back. She was a brave girl so she made herself be brave and she went back to the house. When she returned, the old man was still angry. But this time, he listened to her carefully.
The brave girl told him that she was sorry and that she was alone in the woods. The old man was moved by the brave girl's courage and he decided to forgive her.
He told her that she needed to respect the law and be more careful from now on. The brave girl thanked him and promised to be more careful. The old man then let her go. The brave girl smiled and ran back home feeling very brave and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and a daddy who wanted to go to the market. So, one day, they put on their shoes, got in the car and drove away.
When they got to the market, it was very gloomy. The mommy and daddy looked around and saw lots of people using money to buy things. They bought some food and bought some toys.
When they were done, they put their bags in the car and got back in. But on the way home, the car started to make a noise.
Daddy stopped the car and looked at it. He used some tools and fixed the car so they could get home again. When they got home, they were so glad because they knew they could get back to the market soon!

Once upon a time, there was a lovely little girl named Lily. She had a pet cat named Olive. Lily loved to play with Olive and follow her around the house. Olive was always so soft and cuddly, and Lily loved to pet her.
One day, Lily and Olive went outside to play in the garden. Lily decided to play a game of follow the leader. She would lead and Olive would follow. Lily ran around the garden and Olive chased after her. They had so much fun playing together.
As the sun began to set, Lily picked up Olive and carried her back inside. She gave Olive a big hug and said, "You're my best friend, Olive. I love you." Olive purred and snuggled up to Lily. They both fell asleep, dreaming of all the fun they would have together the next day.

Once upon a time, there was a cheerful pig named Piggie. Piggie loved to play in the mud and eat apples. One day, Piggie's friend Cow came to visit. 
"Hi Piggie!" said Cow. "What are you doing?"
"I'm playing in the mud," said Piggie. "Do you want to play too?"
Cow shook her head. "No, thank you. I don't like to get dirty."
Piggie laughed. "That's okay. I'll cover myself in mud and you can watch!"
Cow watched as Piggie rolled around in the mud. She giggled and said, "You look silly, Piggie."
Piggie smiled. "I know, but it's fun!" 
Cow and Piggie played together all day, and even though Cow didn't want to get dirty, she still had a great time with her cheerful friend.

Once, there was a very rare animal. It had a long, bushy tail like a fox, but it wasn't a fox. It was very, very shy, and almost never let anyone see it. 
One day, a 3 year old girl went out for a walk in the woods. She saw the rare animal hiding behind a tree and said, "Hello, hello! Who are you?" 
"I'm a very rare animal," said the animal, "and I'm very shy. I'm not sure if I can show you my tail, but I am happy to share it with you if you promise to keep it a secret." 
The girl was so excited, she promised not to tell anyone. The rare animal showed her the beautiful scaly tail and they spent the rest of the day playing together.
The girl never forgot her secret friend. She went back to the woods every day looking for the rare animal, but she never found him again.

Once there was a little boy who loved surprises. He asked his mom everyday "what's in the wrap?" But she wouldn't tell him.
One day, the mom had a special surprise for him. She took out a big yellow wrap and said "Do you want to spoil the surprise?". The little boy got so excited that he couldn't say no.
He opened the wrap carefully. Inside was the most beautiful yellow bike he'd ever seen. He was so happy that he hugged his mom and ran outside to show his friends.
The little boy loved his new bike, and rode it every day. It was the best surprise ever!
